summary.text: A 48-year-old man with a 1-month history of fatigue, appetite loss and fever, plus arthralgia, dry cough and mild exertional dyspnea, was admitted. He had a temperature of 37.7°C, heliotrope rash, Gottron's papules, mechanic's hands, palmar papules, facial and back erythema, ulcerative erosive erythema on the elbows, mild proximal lower-limb weakness and edematous hands.

Work-up showed elevated CK, CRP, ferritin, KL-6 and LDH, a high anti-MDA5 antibody titer (>150 indexes), negative anti-ARS, ANA, RF, anti-CCP and ANCA tests, a low PaO2 of 66.4 mmHg on room air, a back skin biopsy with perivascular inflammation and liquefactive degeneration, and reticular shadows with ground-glass opacity on chest CT. He was diagnosed with anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis with rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease.

Methylprednisolone pulse with continuous intravenous cyclosporine A, then oral prednisolone and cyclosporine A, improved systemic symptoms, muscle weakness and CK, but respiratory insufficiency persisted and oxygenation support was required. Intravenous cyclophosphamide 500 mg every 2 weeks for 6 cycles was added, yet respiratory status, chest CT and the hand and elbow ulcerative eruptions worsened despite an additional 750 mg dose.

Rituximab 700 mg weekly for 4 weeks was started on the 125th day of therapy, after which cutaneous lesions, respiratory insufficiency and the radiographic finding improved, ferritin fell to 186 ng/mL and anti-MDA5 antibody to 44 indexes, and the authors report clinical remission.
